about: Ground layers per biome for tools/art/meshy_ground.py. Layer 0 is the base; 1-3 are painted where AmberBiome's weights say (forest: forest floor under the tree masses, path, river mud; desert: hardpan path, oasis grass, sandstone gravel near rock; caribbean: dry beach sand, wet sand, path). mean is the colour the layer should average to, which the ground shader also uses to keep the terrain's own tint. The style reference is a crop of the user's own isometric ground strip (Crowns & Horizons poster, 'Vista en el juego').

forest.name: meadow grass
forest.look: short lush meadow grass with small tufts and a few tiny clover patches

forest.name: forest floor
forest.look: forest floor of fallen brown leaves, moss patches and small twigs

forest.name: dirt path
forest.look: packed brown dirt path with small pebbles and faint wheel ruts

forest.name: river mud

desert.name: hardpan

highland.name: peat bank

volcanic.name: ash plain

volcanic.name: cinder path
volcanic.style: in the same painted game-art style and brushwork as the reference picture, but in a dark volcanic palette of warm ash greys and deep reds, never pure black
volcanic.look: packed path of rust-red volcanic cinder gravel and small dark red pebbles with fine ash in between

volcanic.name: scorched bank
volcanic.style: in the same painted game-art style and brushwork as the reference picture, but in a dark volcanic palette of warm ash greys and deep reds, never pure black
